{{Short description|American computational chemist}}
'''Weston Thatcher Borden'''  (born 1943) is an American chemist with research interests in [[computational chemistry]], [[organic chemistry]], and [[organometallic chemistry]]. He is Distinguished Research Professor Emeritus in chemistry at the [[University of North Texas]], where he was formerly Welch Chair and professor of computational chemistry. He previously taught for many years at the [[University of Washington]]. 

== Early life and education ==
Weston Borden was born in 1943 in [[New York City]],<ref name=ACS2005>{{cite web |first=Sophie |last=Rovner |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/83/i7/2005-ACS-NATIONAL-AWARD-WINNERS.html |title=2005 ACS National Award Winners: Weston T. Borden |work=Chemical & Engineering News |date=February 14, 2005 }}</ref> the son of Martin L. Borden and [[Doris Weston]], who was a singer and a Hollywood star in the 1930s.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=omgtAAAAIBAJ&pg=PA25 |title=Doris Weston, Songstress of 1930s, Dies |newspaper=Schenectady Gazette |date=July 29, 1960 |page=4 |agency=AP }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1960/07/29/archives/doris-westqnbeav-exsingerfms.html |title=Doris Weston Borden: Ex-Singer, Actress |newspaper=The New York Times |date=July 29, 1960 |page=25 }}</ref> He earned bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees from [[Harvard University]],<ref name=ACS2005/><ref name=CV>{{cite web |url=https://chemistry.unt.edu/system/files/weston_thatcher_borden_0.pdf |title=Weston Thatcher Borden: Welch Professor, Theoretical and Organic Chemistry |publisher=University of North Texas, Department of Chemistry |access-date=June 10, 2026 }}</ref> where his Ph.D. dissertation was titled "Electronic structure and geometrical isomerism in allene; some new synthetic routes to an optically active allene".<ref>{{cite thesis |first=Weston Thatcher |last=Borden |title=Electronic structure and geometrical isomerism in allene; some new synthetic routes to an optically active allene |type=Ph.D. |publisher=Harvard University |year=1968 |url=https://id.lib.harvard.edu/alma/990037646340203941/catalog |oclc=1035325606 }}</ref> As a graduate student, he studied [[theoretical chemistry]] at [[Cambridge University]] for a year.<ref name=CV/>

== Career ==
From 1968 to 1973, Borden was an assistant professor at Harvard. He then joined the [[University of Washington]] as an associate professor, where he became a full professor in 1977. He taught there until 2004, when he was appointed as the inaugural [[Robert A. Welch Foundation|Robert A. Welch]] Professor of Chemistry and a professor of computational chemistry at the [[University of North Texas]].<ref name=ACS2005/><ref name=CV/> He was named a Distinguished University Research Professor at the University of North Texas in 2010 and Distinguished Research Professor Emeritus in 2018 following his retirement.<ref name=emeritus>{{cite web |url=https://vpaa.unt.edu/fs/recognition/emeritus-info/emeritus-2018.html |title=2018 Emeritus Recognition |publisher=University of North Texas, Office of the Provost |access-date=June 10, 2026 }}</ref> He was a member of the [[Center for Advanced Scientific Computing and Modeling]], located at the University of North Texas,<ref>Listed as a faculty member for example in [https://web.archive.org/web/20160412081108/https://cascam.unt.edu/ 2016].</ref> and from 1999 was associate editor of the ''Journal of the American Chemical Society''.<ref name=prestigious>{{cite news |url=https://www.ntxe-news.com/cgi-bin/artman/exec/view.cgi?archive=40&num=64691&printer=1 |title=UNT chemistry professor receives prestigious national honor |publisher=University of North Texas news service |date=September 24, 2010 }}</ref>

== Awards ==
Borden has been awarded fellowships by the [[Sloan Foundation]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sloan.org/storage/app/media/files/annual_reports/1974-1978_annual_reports.pdf |title=Report for 1976 |publisher=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |page=27 }}</ref> the [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|Guggenheim Foundation]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows?q=Weston%20T.%20Borden |title=Explore Our Fellows: Weston T. Borden |website=Guggenheim Foundation |access-date=June 10, 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first=Weston Thatcher |last=Borden |title=With a Little Help from My Friends: Forty Years of Fruitful Chemical Collaborations |journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry |volume=76 |issue=9 |date=March 31, 2011 |pages=2943–64 |doi=10.1021/jo200213x }}</ref> the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview/1002855/prof-dr-weston-th-borden |title=Prof. Dr. Weston Th. Borden |website=Alexander von Humboldt Stiftung |access-date=June 10, 2026 }}</ref> and the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]], among others.<ref name=ACS2005/><ref name=CV/><ref name=prestigious/> The [[American Chemical Society]] awarded him a 2005 National Award<ref name=ACS2005/> and the [[James Flack Norris Award]] in Physical Organic Chemistry.<ref name=prestigious/> He was elected a fellow of the Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2005 and was named to the American Chemical Society's inaugural class of fellows in 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://acspss.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/50_60_70_Year-Member-Bios-for-web_2025.pdf |title=Meet The 2025 70, 60 and 50-Year Members |publisher=American Chemical Society Puget Sound chapter |date=2025 |access-date=June 10, 2026 }}</ref><ref name=UNTDaily>{{cite news |first=Kelsey |last=Kruzich |url=https://www.ntdaily.com/archives/american-chemical-society-honors-unt-professor/article_d61cb2bb-0c7d-545f-b5a2-96758503e650.html |title=American Chemical Society honors UNT professor |work=UNT Daily |publisher=University of North Texas |date=October 28, 2009 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Borden and his wife Sheila, also a chemist, have endowed lecture series at the University of Washington (in 2015)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sites.uw.edu/campbelc/calendar_event/borden-lecture-in-theoretical-chemistry-prof-todd-martinez/ |title=Calendar event: Weston and Sheila Borden Endowed Lecture in Theoretical Chemistry: Prof. Todd Martínez |website=University of Washington |date=February 2023 }}</ref> and at the University of North Texas (in 2005, in honor of [[Ernest R. Davidson|Ernest Davidson]]).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cec.mpg.de/en/detail-view/great-honor-for-prof-neese |title=Great honor for Prof. Neese |website=Max Planck Institute for Chemical Energy Conversion |date=April 1, 2015 }}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
